models.label: subloss_v3sel_k5_tgate_deficit_s1
models.hypothesis: Melody-SELECTIVE subspace A/B (C 2026-08-06). Same as the v2 subloss grid but the upweighted 15-dim subspace is now melody-SELECTIVE (whitened CSP: signal=atlas interval deltas, noise=real codec deltas+timbre) instead of top-15 melody-variance. The v2 basis had ~zero melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x) so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody (probable cause of the weak #59); v3 is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. Prediction: v3 arms show more within-clip contour repetition (hook axis) at matched/cleaner texture than the v2 subloss_goa_k arms and the lreq K=1 baseline. Container: lumi-multitorch-full ROCm7 FA2.
models.purpose: The R2(t)-gate mode A/B + seed pairs (CONTINUITY 2026-08-06, burn-day 2026-08-21). Identical to the subspace-loss grid EXCEPT the basis: melody_subspace15_selective_v3 instead of v2. Motivated by the melody machinery-audit — the v2 basis (top-15 melody VARIANCE) had ~ZERO melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x), so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody, the probable reason #59 came back weak. v3 (whitened CSP) is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. K in {2,5,12}, matched to the v2 grid so arms compare directly.

models.label: suomi
models.purpose: CONTROL ARM. Stock Stability training path (plain lora, AdamW, rank 16, lr 1e-4, T256) with the DATASET as the only variable, to determine whether recent widespread model failures come from our additions (FusionOpt / spectral WD / Adagc / forced weight norm / fp32 / s=1 adapters) or from the corpora themselves.
models.hypothesis: If the stock path trains cleanly on a corpus, that corpus is exonerated and the fault is in our stack. If it fails on the same corpora our arms failed on, the fault is in the data.

models.label: subloss_v3sel_k5
models.hypothesis: Melody-SELECTIVE subspace A/B (C 2026-08-06). Same as the v2 subloss grid but the upweighted 15-dim subspace is now melody-SELECTIVE (whitened CSP: signal=atlas interval deltas, noise=real codec deltas+timbre) instead of top-15 melody-variance. The v2 basis had ~zero melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x) so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody (probable cause of the weak #59); v3 is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. Prediction: v3 arms show more within-clip contour repetition (hook axis) at matched/cleaner texture than the v2 subloss_goa_k arms and the lreq K=1 baseline. Container: lumi-multitorch-full ROCm7 FA2.
models.purpose: B1 / #59 — subspace-weighted rectified-flow loss on the v3 melody-selective basis (lumi/melody_subspace15_selective_v3.npz), K in {2,5,12}. An attack on the melody wall.

models.purpose: LR x epoch x weight EQUIVALENCE GRID (CONTINUITY 2026-07-30, Kim greenlit via W; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-lr-steps-weight-equivalence-grid.md). Question: are inference-weight / LR / steps interchangeable along a cumulative-learning axis? The param-space half was already done (‖dW‖ proportional to LR — magnitude invariant; direction cos 0.17-0.47 — flavour diverges). This run supplies the missing pieces: the DIRECTION-MATURITY curve, which needs intermediate checkpoints the adamw sweep never saved, plus the perceptual grid of matched-cumulative triples and weight-for-steps substitution. || The multitorch migration of lr_equiv_grid (CONTINUITY 2026-08-03), moved off sa3.sif because its ROCm 6.2 MIOpen gfx90a find-fallback HANGS. Same experiment as lr_equiv_grid. NOTE arm 1 (lr1e-4) is the shared K=1 BASELINE for the whole melody-wall campaign (subspace / x0-equiv / combined) — do not treat it as a standalone arm. ⚠ AMBIGUOUS KEY: this run-directory name occurs under more than one campaign (lumi/sbatch/lr_equiv_grid.sbatch, lumi/sbatch/lr_equiv_grid_mt.sbatch); the variants above are the candidates and are usually the same experiment ported between containers. Disambiguate by the parent directory before relying on one.

models.label: subloss_goa_k12
models.hypothesis: Spectral-bias counter (arXiv 2503.03206, tau ~ 1/lambda): upweighting the RF error inside the measured 15-dim melody subspace (9.3% of corpus variance) by K forces the gradient to train melodic structure at timbre-like priority; expect more within-clip contour repetition (the hook axis) at matched texture quality. K=1 baseline = lreq_goa_lr1e4. Container: lumi-multitorch-full ROCm7 FA2 (migrated off sa3.sif).
models.purpose: The R2(t)-gate mode A/B + seed pairs (CONTINUITY 2026-08-06, burn-day 2026-08-21). Identical to the subspace-loss grid EXCEPT the basis: melody_subspace15_selective_v3 instead of v2. Motivated by the melody machinery-audit — the v2 basis (top-15 melody VARIANCE) had ~ZERO melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x), so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody, the probable reason #59 came back weak. v3 (whitened CSP) is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. K in {2,5,12}, matched to the v2 grid so arms compare directly.

models.label: x0eq_goa

models.purpose: E1a, the x0-EQUIVALENT LOSS arms (CONTINUITY 2026-07-31, Kim "go on with the tests"). JLT port (arXiv 2605.27102): sigma^2-weighted v-loss == x0-space MSE for a v-output head, removing the isotropic covariance floor that swamps low-variance eigendirections. models.label: lion_lr5e-5-batch32
models.hypothesis: Kim recalled Lion/Prodigy VRAM claims and asked whether Fusion's own optimizer could borrow Prodigy's D-Adaptation trick (auto-discover the right LR scale) cheaply. Implemented as FusionOpt component 'autoscale': a global, model-wide scalar multiplier folded into gamma_t, computed from strided/subsampled (not full-size, unlike real prodigyopt.Prodigy) per-param init-displacement vs gradient-EMA reductions. See _update_autoscale() docstring in fusion_opt.py for the full mechanism.

kim_feedback.verbatim: AdamW is clean but hasn't learned the style terribly well. Fusion at 1e-4 sounds pretty granular and distorted. At 5e-6 the clips sound excellent, and seem to have learned the dataset style very well. actually the clips have such a similar timbre and sub-genre specific style, that I'm wondering if it isn't trained too far, which would be quite a finding with a 10 epoch model that still sounds clean. the clips have a different timbre to AdamW that I can only describe as in your face and forest-punk, IE not like ultra clean progressive trance but more substantial and organic, and just slightly saturated like tape, but not in a bad way.
kim_feedback.ghost_note_note: the lr5e-6 checkpoint listened to is epoch 81 / step 3000 (81 Lightning epochs over the 300-item subset, not literally 10 -- but 81 epochs over 300 tracks is still a small, heavily-repeated dataset, so the overfitting/style-collapse suspicion is well-founded regardless of the exact epoch count Kim recalled). Matches the objective loss-curve finding: fusion-1e-4 was the unstable/spiking arm (audible distortion corroborates the loss spikes to 1.61); fusion-5e-6 was the clean, monotonically-improving arm.
kim_feedback.open_question: does the 5e-6 checkpoint show reduced cross-prompt diversity (same timbre regardless of prompt) vs AdamW -- i.e. is it converging onto one genre/timbre mode rather than following each prompt? Testable via CLAP-embedding pairwise similarity across the 12 different-prompt clips per checkpoint (higher mean similarity = less prompt-following diversity = supports overfitting).

models.recipe: DoRA-rows r128, alpha 128, T=512, lr 5e-5, optimizer Lion, batch 32, 6000 steps; 300-item constrained goa/psytrance subset of latents_sa3. No EMA in the checkpoint (LoRA runs force-disable it), so renders load the online weights.
models.purpose: Second Lion arm of the FusionOpt-autoscale vs AdamW comparison (fusion_autoscale_vs_adamw_2026-09-01): Lion at lr 5e-5 with batch 32, against lion_lr1e-5's lr 1e-5 / batch 8. Same 300-item constrained goa/psytrance subset of latents_sa3 as the rest of the campaign. Trained to 6000 steps (epoch 666); constant LR, no warmup decay visible in metrics.csv. Recipe read from the checkpoint's lora_config + lightning metrics, not from a launcher record -- this run has no run_meta.json on disk.

models.verdict: QUARTER-BATCH test of the 5e-6 arm, sample-matched (12000 bs2 steps = 3000 bs8 steps). lr held at 5e-6 rather than sqrt-scaled to 2.5e-6, deliberately, to test whether autoscale is batch-size robust. models.purpose: 2026-07 (Kim's ear feedback recorded 07-10, docs/checkpoint-hall-of-fame.md; alpha context via docs/dora-alpha-audit-2026-07-12.md): AVP r64 DoRA with alpha=32 (rsLoRA-style, =sqrt(16*64), matched to the r16 baseline) at lr1e-4 -- the lower-LR half of an lr1e-4/lr2e-4 bracket on AVP with TIERED captions, part of both the alpha/rank confound ladder (same family as dora16_avp_8ep/dora128adj_avp_8ep) and (per WORKLOG:625-634) a test of whether caption diversity fixes a 'conditioning collapse' problem found in freeform/single-caption training -- it did (ratio 1.5-2.65 vs freeform's 0.22).

models.label: dora256_avp_aug10_lr7e5
models.verdict: "Arm H" (rank 256) — ruled out after repeated OOM/hang failures on the 16GB card across 4 attempts; this is the lone surviving checkpoint from a run that never completed. Max viable local rank stays 128.
models.purpose: ~2026-07 (before 07-12, exact asker/date not recovered): part of the same alpha/rank confound ladder as dora16_avp_8ep/dora64_avp_tiered/dora128adj (r16->r64->r128->r256, alpha matched via sqrt(16*r) each rung) -- the r256 rung, alpha=64, at a low LR (7e-5), on an early 'aug10' augmented AVP set. CAUTION: do not conflate with the later (07-23) aug10_train.sbatch campaign -- that is a DIFFERENT, fixed-r128 {goa,avp} x {DoRA,fullft} x {fp32,bf16} sweep; the rank/alpha profile here doesn't match it, so this run predates and is unrelated to that campaign despite the shared 'aug10' name fragment.

models.label: dora16_avp_originals_64ep
models.verdict: "D'" — the aug-theory control arm (originals only, no augmentation). Turned out to be the LEAST tempo-stable arm (38% locked), refuting data-multimodality as the tempo-instability driver; instability is optimization-phase/LR-window-driven instead.
models.purpose: AVP r16 DoRA on the 'originals' (non-augmented base) dataset, extended to 64 epochs -- reads as a deliberate overtraining-boundary probe given the extreme epoch count vs the 5-8ep norm elsewhere in this family. WORKLOG.md:2072 (07-22, WINTERMUTE CLAP-degeneration scan) found ep7 of this run already at 44.8% out-of-genre collapse (worst of the rank-16 family, 'overtraining (64ep) worst') -- a post-hoc finding, not launch intent, but consistent with an epoch-ceiling probe.

models.label: dora16_avp_freeform_8ep
models.verdict: Freeform-caption arm — a single descriptive caption did NOT fix conditioning collapse (prompt/seed ratio 0.22, same as the trigger-token baseline's 0.92); showed caption diversity, not caption quality, is what matters.
models.purpose: Part of the same trigger-vs-freeform-vs-tiered-caption conditioning-collapse investigation as dora64_avp_tiered_lr1e4: tests FREEFORM (single descriptive caption, not the fixed trigger token) prompting on AVP r16 DoRA, 8ep. Finding (WORKLOG.md:625-634, post-hoc analysis, names 'the freeform arm'): freeform captions did NOT fix conditioning collapse (ratio 0.22 vs the trigger-token baseline's 0.92) -- established that any single caption reused everywhere collapses conditioning regardless of content, motivating the tiered/diverse-caption fix tested in dora64_avp_tiered.

models.purpose: Part of the same trigger-vs-freeform-vs-tiered-caption conditioning-collapse investigation as dora64_avp_tiered_lr1e4: tests FREEFORM (single descriptive caption, not the fixed trigger token) prompting on AVP r16 DoRA, 8ep. Finding (WORKLOG.md:625-634, post-hoc analysis, names 'the freeform arm'): freeform captions did NOT fix conditioning collapse (ratio 0.22 vs the trigger-token baseline's 0.92) -- established that any single caption reused everywhere collapses conditioning regardless of content, motivating the tiered/diverse-caption fix tested in dora64_avp_tiered.

models.label: lr5e5mixwsd_r128a128_t512_bf16_bs8_s1
models.purpose: Kim direct 2026-08-22 after auditioning the length_variant renders: "the 5e-5 clips sound better than 1e-4, 2e-4 shows degradation, and where 1e-4/2e-4 MELT at cfg16/w2 the 5e-5 can take that push and still sound musical — which speaks to some deeper very healthy structure." So: replicate that run's recipe IN FULL across every sound set we have, to ep48. Replicated run = runs/adamw_bf16_sweep/adamw_goa_t512_bs4_lr5e5 (dora-rows r128 ALPHA 128, AdamW wd0.01, lr 5e-5 CONSTANT, bf16, T512 beat-aware, goa longform sidecar t3 only).

models.label: subloss_v3sel_k5_tgate_deficit_s2
models.purpose: The R2(t)-gate mode A/B + seed pairs (CONTINUITY 2026-08-06, burn-day 2026-08-21). Identical to the subspace-loss grid EXCEPT the basis: melody_subspace15_selective_v3 instead of v2. Motivated by the melody machinery-audit — the v2 basis (top-15 melody VARIANCE) had ~ZERO melody-vs-codec-noise selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x), so upweighting it boosted codec hiss as much as melody, the probable reason #59 came back weak. v3 (whitened CSP) is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise held-out. K in {2,5,12}, matched to the v2 grid so arms compare directly.
